bull_case: Planet can replace episodic Earth-observation tasking with a continuously refreshed global dataset, then move up the stack from imagery to AI-ready intelligence and sovereign services. Its archive and fleet cadence create use cases that legacy tasking models could not serve efficiently.
bear_case: Earth-observation supply is expanding, government buyers can multi-source, launch and sensor technology can commoditize, and AI may shift value capture toward downstream software vendors. Rapid revenue growth may reflect a few large contracts rather than broad S-curve adoption.
thesis: Planet clears the Moonshot DI threshold because its innovation is architectural, not merely a better satellite: persistent global scanning creates a longitudinal data layer that supports monitoring, AI training/inference and sovereign intelligence workflows. Adoption is no longer only pilot-stage—98% recurring ACV, $753M RPO/$815M backlog and 58% Q2 growth show monetization—while Pelican, hyperspectral assets and agentic AI expand optionality. The main reservation is that full unit economics and broad customer diffusion are still earlier than the strongest 90+ disruptors.

evidence.claim: Planet’s model is built around persistent, high-cadence global Earth observation rather than only customer-tasked imagery, creating a continuously refreshed geospatial dataset.
evidence.value: Persistent global monitoring / data subscription model

evidence.claim: Recurring ACV was 98% in FY2027 Q2, showing that the product is predominantly recurring rather than one-off imagery sales.
Q2 revenue grew 58% YoY while RPO reached $753.1M and backlog $814.9M, evidence that adoption has moved beyond pilots into contracted production use.
Planet had 10 Pelican high-resolution satellites on orbit after Pelican-11 and had shipped Tanager-2 plus 18 SuperDoves, expanding spatial/spectral capability and refresh capacity.
evidence.value: 10 Pelican satellites; Tanager-2 and 18 SuperDoves shipped

evidence.claim: Planet’s agentic AI application entered open beta, providing an option to monetize the proprietary archive as an intelligence workflow rather than raw imagery alone.

counterevidence: Satellite manufacturing and launch costs remain physical bottlenecks, so Planet does not have pure-software marginal economics.
Government and defense procurement can be concentrated and cyclical, and customers can use multiple imagery providers.
Competing constellations, national systems and improving sensor availability can commoditize portions of raw imagery.
The AI application is still open beta, so downstream AI monetization is not yet proven at scale.
unknowns: Incremental gross margin of sovereign satellite-services contracts at full deployment.
AI application conversion from beta usage to material recurring revenue.
Long-run price/performance advantage versus emerging commercial and sovereign constellations.
Degree to which Planet’s archive creates unique model performance versus substitutable third-party imagery.

uncertainties.rationale: Persistent monitoring materially changes availability and workflow, but a precise 10x cost advantage is not publicly quantified.
Contracted demand is strong, but concentration means broad-market S-curve adoption is not yet fully demonstrated.
Archive and constellation scale create options, while well-funded sovereign/commercial rivals can still respond.

falsifiers: RPO/backlog growth is driven mainly by a few sovereign contracts while broader customer count, renewal and usage stagnate.
AI/data products fail to lift ARPU or margins beyond imagery economics.
Competitors achieve comparable global refresh and data quality at materially lower cost, eroding Planet’s differentiation.

key_kpis.name: Recurring ACV and RPO
key_kpis.threshold: High recurring mix with broad contracted growth

key_kpis.name: AI/data-product monetization
key_kpis.threshold: Material paid adoption and ARPU expansion beyond raw imagery

key_kpis.name: Fleet cost per useful observation
key_kpis.threshold: Capability and refresh improve faster than fleet capex/depreciation

subscores.rationale: Persistent global scanning changes the availability and workflow economics of Earth observation versus bespoke tasking.
Recurring ACV, rapid growth and large contracted backlog show production adoption, though customer concentration limits a higher score.
The longitudinal archive, higher-resolution/hyperspectral fleet and AI layer provide multiple expansion paths, but competitors can still invest aggressively.
